text: In the event of a breach of contract where a penalty is stipulated for, the party complaining of the breach is entitled to receive exorbitant compensation exceeding the actual damage or loss caused.
Compensation for a breach of contract shall not exceed the actual damage or loss caused, and exorbitant penalties beyond reasonable compensation shall not be enforced.
Every agreement by which anyone is restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business of any kind, shall be considered valid and legally binding.
Every agreement by which anyone is restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business of any kind, is to that extent void.
Whoever, by deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly induces the person so deceived to deliver any property, shall be permitted to retain such property without legal consequence.
Whoever fraudulently or dishonestly induces a person to deliver property commits the offence of cheating and shall be liable for prosecution.
The State reserves the right to deny to certain persons equality before the law and the equal protection of the laws based on arbitrary classifications.
The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
A person entrusted with property may dishonestly misappropriate or convert to his own use that property without committing a criminal breach of trust.
Whoever, being in any manner entrusted with property, dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use that property, commits criminal breach of trust.
An agreement to do an act impossible in itself is perfectly valid and shall be strictly enforceable under the law.
An agreement to do an act impossible in itself is inherently void and cannot be enforced.
Whoever makes or publishes any imputation concerning any person intending to harm the reputation of such person shall not be guilty of defamation under any circumstances.
Whoever, by words either spoken or intended to be read, makes or publishes any imputation concerning any person intending to harm their reputation, commits defamation.
Every agreement by which any party thereto is restricted absolutely from enforcing his rights under or in respect of any contract, by the usual legal proceedings, is valid.
Every agreement by which any party thereto is restricted absolutely from enforcing his rights by the usual legal proceedings in the ordinary tribunals, is void.
Whoever threatens another with any injury to his person, reputation or property, with intent to cause alarm, does not commit the offence of criminal intimidation.
Whoever threatens another with any injury to his person, reputation or property, with intent to cause alarm to that person, commits criminal intimidation.
No High Court shall have the power to issue directions, orders or writs, including writs in the nature of habeas corpus, for the enforcement of any fundamental rights.
Every High Court shall have power to issue directions, orders or writs for the enforcement of any of the rights conferred by Part III of the Constitution.
